title: Stop generating Wasm bindings into packages/; generate them directly into the consuming app's own build output at build/install time
objective: Owner-directed (chat, confirmed via AskUserQuestion, refined twice more via follow-up chat corrections): packages/isekai-wasm and packages/vtt-generation-wasm were npm 'technical packages' whose entire content was wasm-pack's generated output from libs/isekai/wasm-bridge and libs/vtt/generation-wasm. Final confirmed design (superseding two earlier attempts -- an Nx target on the consuming app, then a plain package.json script chained into build/dev -- both explicitly rejected by the owner): each Wasm-producing Rust crate under libs/ gets its own co-located package.json (npm name unchanged from before, e.g. @grafting/isekai-wasm, @grafting/vtt-generation-wasm -- 'isekai' stays in the isekai bridge's package name specifically to signal it is the multiplatform interop boundary) with a postinstall script running wasm-pack straight into that same directory (e.g. libs/isekai/wasm-bridge/pkg/, gitignored). Consuming apps depend on it as a completely normal workspace:* dependency in package.json's dependencies -- no custom script, no Nx target/project.json wiring for this at all; a plain pnpm install already performs the conversion, 'like a normal project'. apps/architecture-studio's Worker files (layout.worker.ts, generation.worker.ts) switch from runtime-URL static-asset fetching to a normal static import of the workspace package, letting Next.js's own bundler resolve/package the .wasm (flagged risk: an earlier spike in this repo specifically avoided static-importing wasm-bindgen output inside a Next.js-bundled Worker for concrete empirical reasons -- must be reverified working, not assumed, during this task's verification step; fall back to the runtime-fetch pattern if it breaks). packages/isekai-web-client reverts to its original static-import design against @grafting/isekai-wasm (now co-located in libs/, not packages/) since it is a normal dependency again. Full history in the approved plan at C:\Users\PICHAU\.claude\plans\mellow-drifting-nova.md.
validations: DONE: implemented and reverted two earlier designs in direct response to owner corrections before landing on the final one -- (1) an Nx `wasm-generate` target on apps/architecture-studio/project.json, rejected ('instead of via nx... like a normal package... without me having to keep generating in project.json'); (2) a plain package.json `wasm:generate` script chained into build/dev, rejected ('just in dependencies, nothing else, like a normal project'). Confirmed the final shape explicitly via AskUserQuestion before implementing it a third time.

DONE: libs/isekai/wasm-bridge/package.json and libs/vtt/generation-wasm/package.json created, co-located with each crate's Cargo.toml, each with a `postinstall` script running `wasm-pack build --target web --out-dir pkg`. Ran a real `pnpm install` at the workspace root and confirmed both postinstall scripts fired automatically (no allowlist/config change needed for first-party workspace packages) and produced real pkg/ output (grafting_isekai_wasm.js/.d.ts/.wasm, grafting_vtt_generation_wasm.js/.d.ts/.wasm) inside each crate's own directory, not packages/.

DONE: deleted packages/isekai-wasm/ and packages/vtt-generation-wasm/ entirely (package.json, README.md, AGENTS.md, gitignored pkg/); confirmed via regenerated docs/generated/repo-map.md diff that the implicit '@grafting/isekai-wasm | packages/isekai-wasm' Nx project entry is gone (14->15 named/typed projects, the untyped placeholder row removed).

DONE: removed the `build` target (wasm-pack invocation) from libs/isekai/wasm-bridge/project.json and libs/vtt/generation-wasm/project.json; deleted apps/architecture-studio/scripts/copy-wasm-assets.mjs and its two npm-script invocations; apps/architecture-studio/package.json now has zero wasm-pack/copy-script mentions, just @grafting/isekai-wasm and @grafting/vtt-generation-wasm as plain workspace:* dependencies.

DONE (flagged risk, reverified not assumed): switched apps/architecture-studio/src/layout.worker.ts and src/app/lab/generation.worker.ts from the runtime static-asset-fetch pattern to a normal static `import ... from "@grafting/isekai-wasm"` / "@grafting/vtt-generation-wasm", per the owner's explicit choice after being warned this reopens a question spikes/wasm-worker-nextjs previously closed empirically. Ran `pnpm run build` (next build, Turbopack) for architecture-studio: compiled successfully, tsc clean, all 7 routes (including /lab, the generation-wasm consumer) generated; confirmed via `find .next -iname *wasm*` that Turbopack resolved and copied both .wasm binaries into its static asset output (content-hashed, both dev and prod builds) -- real evidence the static import resolves and bundles correctly at build time. Not independently verified at Worker runtime in an actual browser (no browser-automation tool available this session, same limitation noted in the prior ARCH-STUDIO-STORYBOOK-SAMEORIGIN-PROXY task) -- recorded as a residual risk, not silently assumed safe.

DONE: reverted packages/isekai-web-client's src/protocol.ts, src/worker.ts, src/index.ts, package.json, test/browser-check.html, test/basic.test.ts back to their pre-task static-import design (git diff confirms zero net change on these files) once @grafting/isekai-wasm became a normal workspace package again -- the earlier wasmUrl-parameter redesign (built for the second, rejected app-owned-script design) was fully unwound, not left as dead code.

risks: The static-import Worker change (layout.worker.ts, generation.worker.ts) is verified working at build time (next build/Turbopack compiles clean, both .wasm binaries land in the static asset output) but not independently verified at Worker runtime in an actual browser -- no browser-automation tool was available this session. If a real browser later surfaces the failure mode spikes/wasm-worker-nextjs originally found, the documented rollback in ADR-0017 is to revert just these two files to the runtime static-asset-fetch pattern, not to reopen the rest of this decision.

wasm-pack now runs on every `pnpm install` for any workspace member depending on these two crates (in practice, any full-workspace install, since apps/architecture-studio depends on both) -- this requires the Rust toolchain and wasm-pack to be present wherever `pnpm install` runs, including CI. Not yet reflected in any environment-setup documentation beyond this task record and ADR-0017's own 'Follow-up work' section.

This investigation/implementation only proves the current working tree is internally consistent and passes every local check -- none of this session's substantial uncommitted changes (this task included) have been committed or pushed yet, so the real CI on master is unaffected either way until that happens.
